verdict: Caution: lend selectively to Raigarh power value-chain borrowers with strong offtake and receivable discipline; avoid pure merchant/spot-exposed and discom-dependent exposures until local demand and GST trends improve.
title: Raigarh Power Generation & Distribution: a note to the credit manager
narrative:
## What this business physically is
**Power generation converts coal into units sold under PPAs; cash arrives from discoms, not from the plant gate.** In Raigarh the anchor is Adani Power's Raigarh Phase-II, under execution alongside Korba, Mahan, Raipur, Mirzapur and Anuppur [1]. Nationally, coal and lignite met 73% of incremental generation in Q2 FY27 and average thermal PLF rose to 68% from 62% [1]. **So when a proposal lands, check the PPA share first; if offtake is merchant/spot, ask for the counterparty and tenure.**

## Where value and cash sit
**Value sits in long-tenure PPAs and fuel logistics; cash sits in the receivable, and that is where the risk lives.** Adani Power has secured long-term PPAs for 62% of its 24 GW thermal pipeline [1]; 95% of its operating capacity is tied to long-term PPAs [5]. Counterparty risk is real: one peer's average collection period extended beyond 400 days in FY25 from 351 days, with debtors at Rs 5,020 crore as of June 30, 2025 [8]. **So take the receivable ageing every month; if days exceed the customer's stated norm, ask for the discom payment trail and LC/escrow cover.**

## What has changed now
**The local demand signal is weaker than India's, so do not underwrite Raigarh on national growth.** Chhattisgarh electricity demand rose 6.7% Apr-to-date against India's 9.5% [D], and state GST collections grew 2.4% against India's 6.1% [D]. Nationally, bank credit grew 22.9% YoY against activity of 9.5%, a 13.4 pp gap [D]. **So when a borrower shows rapid revenue growth, check whether it is funded by bank credit faster than units sold; if yes, ask for the unit-sales reconciliation.**

## Where to grow, and how to grow safely
**Pursue contractors and equipment suppliers to the Raigarh Phase-II and Raipur expansion, and O&M/fuel-logistics vendors with assigned PPA receivables.** Adani Power is adding a third Raipur phase of 1,600 MW, expanding the site to 4,570 MW [1]. Peer results are mixed: Vedanta Power reported record quarterly sales with EBITDA up 45% sequentially and margins at 14.5% [3], and separately 122% EBITDA growth to INR 421 crore on revenue of INR 2,908 crore [4]; Coal India's Q2 FY27 net profit rose 57% YoY to Rs 6,547 crore even as target prices were cut [2]. **Avoid pure merchant generators and borrowers whose sole comfort is a discom receivable; if the borrower's cash flow waterfall lacks a DSRA, ask for one before sanction** [6]. ## Early-warning signs
**Watch receivable days, PLF, and PPA share together; any two moving the wrong way is a red flag.** Rating commentary flags collection-period extension and debtor build-up as the first sign of counterparty stress [8]. **Take monthly: unit generation, PLF, receivable ageing, DSRA balance and working-capital limit utilisation** [6]. Note the rating sources [6][7][8][9] are undated and [7] is from March 2016, so treat them as method guidance, not current fact. Sources say little about Raigarh specifically; lean on first principles and peers.
watch: Above the customer's stated norm -> ask for discom payment trail and LC/escrow
PLF falls below the borrower's budget -> re-run cash flow and resize limits
Merchant/spot share rises -> require assignment of PPA receivables
Below stipulated minimum -> stop fresh disbursement until topped up
watch_note: Trigger levels are policy suggestions (analytical framing), not data.
